The refuter correctly identified that the old title and statement overclaimed a strict gap between the countable and finite partition suprema. The current item now narrows the refutation to failure of finite attainment and proves exactly that with the e^(ix) density example.

The refuter correctly identified that the old signed-measure definition left |nu(E_n)| undefined at +/-infty. The current definition now explicitly interprets infinite signed-measure values as contributing +infty to the partition sum, so the formula is typed on the live carrier.

The refuter correctly identified that the old weighted sum allowed undefined terms such as i*(+infty) or 0*(+infty). The current definition now restricts to the nonzero level sets of finite total variation, which makes every term a finite real or complex number.

The refuter correctly identified that the old pair {1},{-1} was not a Hahn decomposition because it did not partition R. The current example now uses the genuine Hahn partition P=R\{-1}, N={-1}, and the Jordan measures follow exactly on the live text.

The refuter correctly identified that the old closed-quadrant grouping let boundary values land in two A_q at once. Step 1.1 now assigns each z_n to the least admissible quadrant index, making the A_q a disjoint partition while preserving the estimate.

The refuter correctly identified the unique bad logarithm index where lambda+2pi i k vanishes. The current proof now excludes that single integer and still produces infinitely many z_k -> 0 with f(z_k)=w.

The refuter correctly identified that the old quadratic-formula expression was applied at w=0, where it became 0/0. The current proof now treats w=0 separately and uses the quadratic formula only for w != 0.

The refuter correctly identified that the old theorem used Montel without carrying the Choice hypothesis named in the cited normal-family theorem. The current statement and facts block now assume the Axiom of Choice exactly where the subsequence extraction is used.

The refuter correctly identified that the old proof cited the area line-integral theorem without first producing the finite elementary decomposition that theorem requires. The current proof now constructs that decomposition explicitly before the area integral step.

The refuter correctly identified that the old theorem invoked the chordal Arzela-Ascoli criterion without carrying the Choice hypothesis named in the cited theorem. The current statement and facts block now make the Axiom of Choice explicit before using the normality criterion.
The refuter correctly identified that the old final sentence conflated length M with pole order M. The current definition now says the order is at most M and is exactly M only when c_-M != 0.

The refuter correctly identified that the old geometric-series inequality |a_{j-1}-a_j| < |z-a_j| does not follow from common membership in a disc disjoint from K. The current proof now uses the open/closed one-disc pole-pushing argument and then iterates it along the chain.

The refuter correctly identified that the old radius choice |a_n| < R_n < |a_{n+1}| fails when the enumeration has repeated moduli. The current proof now groups the discrete pole set into finite radial shells and applies polynomial approximation shell by shell.

The refuter correctly identified that the old step 2.1 applied the plane-domain Runge theorem to f_n even though f_n was only holomorphic near K_{n-1}, not on all of Omega. The current proof now builds the exhaustion explicitly and invokes the compact prescribed-pole Runge theorem on each K_{n-1}.

The refuter correctly identified that the old bounded-strip argument never justified pole cancellation inside the strip. The current proof replaces that step with the residue-theorem rectangle argument and derives the symmetric partial fractions directly.

The refuter correctly identified that the old upper/lower-ray orientation calculation produced the wrong sign in front of 2i sin(pi z) Gamma(1-z). The current step 2.1 recomputes the ray contributions with the repository's Hankel orientation and obtains the positive sign required by the reflection formula.

The refuter correctly identified that the old first logarithmic rewrite had the wrong sign pattern and did not match the reciprocal-Gamma product. The current proof now derives the correct Binet-type formula from the product, harmonic asymptotics, and real Stirling before estimating the remainder integral.
